findings.summary: Traditional 2D animation creates the illusion of motion by drawing each frame by hand on transparent cels, which are then photographed over static backgrounds. The process begins with storyboards and scripts, followed by voice recording and design phases. Key animators draw major poses, and assistant animators fill in the gaps through inbetweening. Drawings are traced onto cels, inked, and painted on the reverse side before being layered and photographed frame-by-frame using a rostrum camera. Digital ink and paint now combines hand-drawn elements with computer compositing.

mechanisms.title: Frame-by-frame hand drawing
mechanisms.explanation: Animators draw sequences on perforated transparent paper fitted to peg bars, creating key frames and pencil tests to review motion before passing to assistants who add missing frames via inbetweening.

mechanisms.title: Cel transfer and layering
mechanisms.explanation: Approved drawings are traced onto transparent plastic cels, inked on the outline, and painted on the reverse side. These cels are layered over backgrounds and photographed frame-by-frame using a rostrum camera to produce the final image.

unknowns: Exact frame rate determination method per scene
